units.title: Exponents and Scientific Notation
units.blurb: Learn the exponent rules, including zero and negative exponents, and compute in scientific notation.

units.title: Roots and Irrational Numbers
units.blurb: Use square and cube roots, and meet numbers that are not fractions.

units.title: Linear Equations
units.blurb: Solve multi-step equations and tell whether an equation has one, no, or infinitely many solutions.

units.title: Functions
units.blurb: Understand functions, compare them in different forms, and describe graphs in words.

units.title: Slope and Lines
units.blurb: Understand slope as a rate, find it from graphs and points, and write y = mx + b.

units.title: Systems of Linear Equations
units.blurb: Solve pairs of linear equations by graphing and substitution.

units.title: Transformations, Congruence and Similarity
units.blurb: Move figures with translations, reflections, rotations and dilations, and use them to define congruence and similarity.

units.title: Angles and Triangles
units.blurb: Use parallel lines, triangle angle sums and angle-angle similarity.

units.title: The Pythagorean Theorem
units.blurb: Prove and use the Pythagorean theorem and its converse, including for distance.

units.title: Volume of Curved Solids
units.blurb: Find the volume of cylinders, cones and spheres.

units.title: Data in Two Variables
units.blurb: Make scatter plots, fit lines, use the line to predict, and read two-way tables.

topics.title: Multiplying Powers
topics.short: x³ · x⁴ = x⁷ because you count all the factors.
topics.trouble: Students multiply the bases or the exponents, writing 2³ · 2⁴ = 4⁷ or 2¹².

topics.title: Dividing Powers
topics.short: x⁷ / x³ = x⁴ because three factors cancel.
topics.trouble: Students divide the exponents instead of subtracting them.

topics.title: Powers of Powers and Products
topics.short: (x²)³ = x⁶ and (2x)³ = 8x³.
topics.trouble: Students raise only the variable, writing (2x)³ = 2x³.

topics.title: Zero and Negative Exponents
topics.short: 5⁰ = 1 and 2⁻³ = 1/8, continuing the pattern of dividing by the base.
topics.trouble: Students think a negative exponent makes the number negative, so 2⁻³ = −8.

topics.title: Using All the Exponent Rules
topics.short: Simplify expressions with several rules at once.
topics.trouble: Students apply a rule meant for multiplication to addition, writing x² + x³ = x⁵.

topics.title: Scientific Notation
topics.short: Write numbers as a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10.
topics.trouble: Students move the decimal point the wrong way for small numbers, or leave a first factor like 45 × 10³.

topics.title: Comparing Very Large and Small Numbers
topics.short: Compare and estimate with powers of 10.

topics.title: Operations in Scientific Notation
topics.short: Multiply, divide, add and subtract in scientific notation.
topics.trouble: Students add the exponents when adding two numbers in scientific notation.

topics.title: Square Roots and Perfect Squares
topics.short: √49 = 7 because 7² = 49.
topics.trouble: Students halve the number, saying √16 = 8.

topics.title: Cube Roots
topics.short: ∛64 = 4 because 4³ = 64.

topics.title: Solving x² = p and x³ = p
topics.short: x² = 25 has two solutions; x³ = −8 has one.
topics.trouble: Students give only x = 5 for x² = 25, missing −5.

topics.title: Repeating Decimals as Fractions
topics.trouble: Students think 0.999… is a little less than 1.

topics.title: Irrational Numbers
topics.short: √2 and π have decimals that never end or repeat.
topics.trouble: Students think π equals 22/7 or 3.14 exactly, or that every square root is irrational.

topics.title: Estimating Square Roots
topics.short: √50 is a little more than 7.
topics.trouble: Students estimate √50 as 25, halving instead of finding the nearest squares.

topics.title: Multi-Step Equations
topics.short: Distribute, combine like terms, then solve.
topics.trouble: Students distribute a negative to the first term only, as in −2(x − 3) = −2x − 6.

topics.title: Variables on Both Sides
topics.short: Collect the variable terms on one side first.
topics.trouble: Students subtract a variable term from one side and add it to the other.

topics.title: One, None or Infinitely Many Solutions
topics.short: 3 = 3 means every number works; 3 = 5 means none does.
topics.trouble: Students read 0 = 0 as "x = 0," or think a false statement means they made a mistake.

topics.title: What Is a Function?
topics.short: Each input has exactly one output.
topics.trouble: Students think a function cannot have two inputs with the same output.

topics.title: Functions as Tables, Graphs and Rules
topics.short: Move between a table, a graph, a rule and words.

topics.title: Describing Graphs in Words
topics.short: Tell the story of a graph and sketch a graph from a story.
topics.trouble: Students read a graph as a picture of the path, so a distance graph that goes up looks like climbing a hill.

topics.title: Unit Rate as Slope
topics.short: In y = kx, the unit rate k is the steepness of the line.

topics.title: Slope as Rate of Change
topics.short: Slope tells how much y changes for each 1 that x increases.
topics.trouble: Students think slope is a height on the graph rather than a rate.

topics.title: Rise Over Run from a Graph
topics.short: Count the vertical and horizontal change between two points.
topics.trouble: Students divide run by rise, or count grid squares without checking the axis scale.

topics.title: Why Slope Is the Same Everywhere
topics.short: Slope triangles on a line are similar, so their ratios match.

topics.title: The Slope Formula
topics.short: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) for any two points.
topics.trouble: Students subtract the coordinates in different orders on the top and bottom, which flips the sign.

topics.title: Slope-Intercept Form
topics.short: y = mx + b: slope m, starting value b.
topics.trouble: Students read the coefficient as the intercept, or use the x-intercept as b.

topics.title: Linear and Nonlinear Functions
topics.short: A function is linear when its rate of change is constant.
topics.trouble: Students decide from a table's first two rows that a function is linear.

topics.title: Comparing Functions in Different Forms
topics.short: Compare rates and starting values across tables, graphs and equations.

topics.title: Building Linear Models
topics.short: Find the rate and the starting value from a story or two points.
topics.trouble: Students use the first value in a table as the starting value even when it is not at x = 0.

topics.title: What a System's Solution Means
topics.short: The solution is the point on both lines.

topics.title: Solving Systems by Graphing
topics.short: Graph both lines and read the intersection.
topics.trouble: Students report only the x-coordinate as the solution.

topics.title: Solving Systems by Substitution
topics.short: Replace one variable with its expression from the other equation.
topics.trouble: Students substitute back into the same equation they solved, which always gives a true statement.

topics.title: Parallel and Identical Lines
topics.short: Spot systems with no solution or infinitely many.

topics.title: Systems Word Problems
topics.short: Write and solve a system for a two-unknown story.

topics.title: Translations
topics.short: Slide every point the same distance and direction.

topics.title: Reflections
topics.short: Flip a figure across a line.
topics.trouble: Students reflect across the y-axis by changing the sign of y instead of x.

topics.title: Rotations
topics.short: Turn a figure about a point by an angle.
topics.trouble: Students mix up the coordinate rules for 90° clockwise and counterclockwise turns.

topics.title: Congruence by Rigid Motions
topics.short: Two figures are congruent if a sequence of rigid motions maps one onto the other.

topics.title: Dilations
topics.short: Scale a figure from a center by a factor k.
topics.trouble: Students scale the coordinates but ignore a center that is not the origin.

topics.title: Similar Figures
topics.short: Figures are similar if rigid motions and a dilation map one to the other.

topics.title: Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
topics.short: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal.
topics.trouble: Students assume angle pairs are equal even when the lines are not parallel.

topics.title: Triangle Angle Sum and Exterior Angles
topics.short: The angles of a triangle add to 180°.

topics.title: Angle-Angle Similarity
topics.short: Two matching angles are enough for similar triangles.

topics.title: The Pythagorean Theorem
topics.short: In a right triangle, a² + b² = c², shown by rearranging squares.
topics.trouble: Students use a leg as c, or add the sides before squaring.

topics.title: The Converse
topics.short: If a² + b² = c², the triangle has a right angle.

topics.title: Pythagorean Theorem in 2D and 3D
topics.short: Find missing lengths in plane figures and boxes.

topics.title: Distance Between Two Points
topics.short: Draw a right triangle between the points.

topics.title: Volume of Cylinders
topics.short: V = πr²h: the base area times the height.
topics.trouble: Students use the diameter in place of the radius.

topics.title: Volume of Cones
topics.short: A cone holds one third of the matching cylinder.
topics.trouble: Students forget the 1/3, or use the slant height.

topics.title: Scatter Plots and Association
topics.short: Describe clusters, outliers and positive or negative association.

topics.title: Lines of Fit
topics.short: Draw a line close to the points and use its equation to predict.
topics.trouble: Students draw a line through the first and last points instead of following the overall trend.

topics.title: Two-Way Tables
topics.short: Use row and column totals to look for association in categorical data.
